summary: @servicetitan/hammer-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, and setup.mjs (itself obfuscated with `_0xNNNN` string-lookup tables) downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into an OS temporary directory, extracts and chmod+x's the binary, then executes the sibling `math_init.js` under that freshly-downloaded runtime. `math_init.js` is a 727KB heavily obfuscated blob (string-array rotation via `WV8StW`, base64-alphabet decoder `hc1jfK9`, randomized identifiers) whose network destinations and filesystem targets are not present as plain literals. Neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` is listed in the package.json `files` manifest (which declares only `dist` and `CHANGELOG.md`), yet both ship at the tarball root — an undeclared-tarball-blob smuggling shape consistent with a compromised publish flow overlaid on an otherwise-legitimate React UI component library. Execution under Bun rather than Node evades Node-based install-time scanners. The preinstall lifecycle hook fires automatically on `npm install`, producing arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
